author: O. Henry
attribution: 据欧·亨利 1906 年短篇改写 · PET 分级试读
intro: 二十年前，他们在纽约一家餐馆道别。今晚十点，约定还算数吗？

watch.meaning: n. 表，随身的报时工具

on time.meaning: 短语　准时，按约定时间

made my money.meaning: 在这里指挣下了自己的家产

wanted.meaning: 在这里指警方正在通缉

pages.en: A police officer walked along a New York street, trying the shop doors. It was nearly ten. The wind had driven almost everyone indoors. Halfway down the street, a man stood in a dark [[doorway]]. He had a cigar in his mouth, but it wasn't lit.
pages.zh: 快十点了。一名巡警走在纽约街上，挨家推推店门。风把行人都赶进了屋。走到街道中段，只见一名男子站在黑洞洞的门口，嘴里叼着一支没点着的雪茄。

pages.en:
Before the officer could ask a question, the man began to explain. “I have an [[appointment]] here tonight. A rather old one. When we made it, this shop was a [[restaurant]].”

“Big Joe Brady's,” he added.

“Yes,” said the officer. “They pulled it down five years ago.”
pages.zh:
巡警还没开口，那人就解释起来。“我今晚约了人在这儿见面。约得有点早。我们定下日子的时候，这家店还是间餐馆呢。”

“大乔·布雷迪开的。”他又说。

“对，”巡警说，“五年前拆的。”

questions.en: Why is the man waiting outside a closed shop?
questions.zh: 这家关门的店为什么值得他等？
options: He promised to meet someone at this spot.
He expects the owner to open the shop.
He has arranged to meet the officer.
questions.reason: 餐馆已经拆了，约定见面的地点却仍是这里。

pages.en:
The man struck a [[match]]. For a second its [[light]] showed a white [[scar]] near his right eyebrow and a diamond at his throat.

“Jimmy Wells and I grew up here together,” he said. “At our last dinner I was eighteen. Jimmy was twenty. Next morning I went west. Jimmy wouldn't leave New York for anything.”
pages.zh:
那人划了根火柴。火光闪了一下，照见他右眉旁一道白疤，还有领口的一颗钻石。

“吉米·韦尔斯跟我是在这儿一块儿长大的。最后一次同桌吃饭，我十八，他二十。第二天我就去了西部。吉米呢，说什么也不肯离开纽约。”

pages.en:
“We gave ourselves twenty years. Then we'd come back and see how life had turned out.” They wrote for a year or two. After that, nothing.

He opened his fine [[watch]]. “Nine fifty-seven. We said goodbye at ten.”

“And if he's late?” asked the officer.

“I've come a thousand miles. I'll wait at least another half hour.” The officer wished him good night and walked on.
pages.zh:
“我们给了彼此二十年。到时候再回来，看看对方过得怎样。”头一两年他们还通信，后来就断了。

他掀开那块精致的表。“九点五十七。我们那晚十点道的别。”

“要是他迟到了呢？”巡警问。

“一千英里我都来了。少说也再等半个钟头。”巡警道了晚安，继续往前走。

questions.en: What lets the officer see the man's face?
questions.zh: 巡警是借着什么看清那张脸的？
options: A light inside the shop.
A match the man uses for his cigar.
The glass on the man's watch.
questions.reason: 男子自己点雪茄，脸才在那一瞬间亮了起来。

questions.en: What makes his decision to wait remarkable?
questions.zh: 他肯继续等，这件事为什么格外有分量？
options: Jimmy wrote to him that morning.
He lives next door and has time to spare.
They lost touch years ago, yet he made the journey.
questions.reason: 两人早已断了音信。他仍为那个老约定走了一千英里。

pages.en:
A cold rain began to fall. About twenty minutes later, a tall man hurried across the street. The [[collar]] of his long coat came up almost to his ears.

“Bob?” he called.

“Jimmy Wells!” said the man in the doorway. The tall man took both his hands.
pages.zh:
冷雨落了下来。约莫二十分钟后，一个高个子快步穿过街道，长外套的领子竖得几乎碰到了耳朵。

“鲍勃？”他喊道。

门口的人叫了起来：“吉米·韦尔斯！”高个子握住了他的双手。

pages.en:
“If only the old place were still here,” the tall man said. “We could have dinner again. How was the West?”

“I [[made my money]] there. But look at you, Jimmy. I don't remember you being this tall.”

“A man can still grow a little after twenty.” He offered Bob his arm. They walked off [[arm in arm]], Bob eager to tell him about his life.
pages.zh:
“老店要是还在就好了，咱俩还能再吃上一顿。西部怎么样？”高个子问。

“我在那儿挣下了家业。可是吉米，我记得你没这么高啊。”

“过了二十岁，也还会再长一点嘛。”他把胳膊递给鲍勃。两人挽着手臂往前走，鲍勃急着讲这些年的经历。

questions.en: Which detail surprises Bob even while he welcomes the man?
questions.zh: 鲍勃高兴归高兴，有哪个细节让他觉得奇怪？
options: The man seems taller than he remembers.
The man has forgotten his name.
The man refuses to talk about their old restaurant.
questions.reason: 对方叫得出他的名字，也提起了老餐馆。鲍勃记忆里对不上的，是身高。

pages.en:
On the corner, a drugstore window lit up the pavement. The two men turned to look at each other. Now Bob could see the stranger's whole [[face]]. He dropped the man's arm.

“You aren't Jimmy. Twenty years might change a lot. They wouldn't give a man a different [[nose]].”
pages.zh:
街角药店的橱窗把人行道照得通亮。两人转过头看对方。鲍勃这才看清身旁那人的整张脸。他一下子松开了手。

“你不是吉米。二十年能改变不少事，可不会把一个人的鼻子换个样子。”

pages.en:
“They can change an honest man,” the other man said. “You've been [[under arrest]] for ten minutes, Bob. The Chicago police have been looking for you.”

Before taking him to the police station, the man handed Bob a folded [[note]]. He told him he could read it there, by the window. It was from an officer named Wells.
pages.zh:
“二十年也能改变一个正派人。”对方说，“鲍勃，十分钟前你就已经被捕了。芝加哥警方一直在找你。”

去警局前，那人递给鲍勃一张折好的便条，让他就着橱窗的灯读。写便条的是一位姓韦尔斯的警官。

questions.en: Why does Bob let go at the drugstore?
questions.zh: 在药店门口，鲍勃为什么突然松手？
options: He sees the Chicago police waiting inside.
He can finally see a feature that doesn't fit his memory.
He has already read what is in the note.
questions.reason: 先有橱窗的光，鲍勃才看清鼻子的样子。便条是他松手之后才收到的。

pages.en:
Bob opened the piece of paper. His hand was perfectly still.

“Dear Bob, I kept our appointment. I was there [[on time]]. In the flash of your match I saw the man [[wanted]] by the Chicago police. I couldn't bring myself to arrest you. I found another officer in [[plain clothes]] and asked him to do it for me.

Jimmy”

By the time Bob reached the name at the bottom, the paper was shaking a little in his hand.
pages.zh:
鲍勃展开纸条，手稳稳的。

“鲍勃，我赴约了，准时到的。你的火柴一亮，我就认出了芝加哥警方通缉的那个人。我实在没法亲手逮捕你，就找了个穿便衣的警官，让他替我办这件事。

吉米”

读到末尾的署名时，那张纸在鲍勃手里微微抖了起来。

questions.en: Did Jimmy keep his appointment with Bob?
questions.zh: 当年的约定，吉米究竟赴了吗？
options: No. He only sent a note from Chicago.
Yes. He was the tall man outside the drugstore.
Yes. He had already spoken to Bob as the first officer.
questions.reason: 吉米在便条里说自己准时到了，还提到火柴亮起的一刻。当时站在鲍勃面前的，正是第一位巡警。

questions.en: Why did Jimmy ask someone else to make the arrest?
questions.zh: 为什么吉米要找另一个人来？
options: He recognised his friend and could not bear to arrest him himself.
He needed someone to tell him whether the man was Bob.
He hoped the second officer would let Bob go.
questions.reason: 纸条里，吉米承认自己认出了鲍勃，也承认自己下不了手。他还是请同事履行了警察的职责。
